bench.warm_note: as PL-SMT rp4: tcl/bdc accumulators (no-reset data cuts) take power-up / pre-epoch values until a protocol i_first; landed children see them t(child) edges later, so random stimulus needs a flush window before the compare

why: HF-5c 10-18: HBM SM attention cluster ot_hbm_accel_smh_attn (x16 on d4g) as a LANDED PARENT: 17 regions = front + one per attn tile (each ~1.6 mm tall); BE with its column's row-pair-1 tile. Front split into launch/result nodes so the q return chain is not a loop.

compiler_note.loop_resolution: The flat-node loop front -> tiles -> BE -> q chain -> front is broken STRUCTURALLY: ot_smh_static_front's result path (ql/qr lane landing, (5+PT4+PINR)-per-hop deskew, result_valid, rv/rrow/rdata/fault) reads ONLY ql/qr, and nothing on its launch side (feed, fc_*, rl/rr/bl/br, expected_request, schedule_fault) reads ql/qr; the attention front's fault is the static front's fault. So the front is two lp nodes: u_fl (ot_hbm_sm_attn_front_launch, t 0) and u_fr (ot_smh_static_front_result, t 27). No compiler re-schedule needed for the loop.
compiler_note.schedule_change: Command / packet / kv_desc / xw inputs and request / schedule_fault: offset 0 (unchanged calendar). Results rv / rrow / rdata / fault: +27 edges = 9 landed hops x (E+1 = 3): front -> nearest tile (3), 3 column hops out (9), row-pair 0 -> row-pair 1 gather (3), 3 BE q-chain hops back (9), nearest BE -> front result (3). sm_elem_bench 'out' latency (and every SM result consumer) adds 27; the QK landing / PV node calendar inside the SM is unchanged because every child runs t(child) edges late with its reset run (lockstep).
compiler_note.deskew_equivalent: Equivalently per landed column hop the outbound rows take +3 and the returning q lane +3: the front's result deskew per hop (5+PT4+PINR) would become (5+PT4+PINR)+6 if the BE gin pads (t*_go -> u_be*, 6/12/18 stages x 200 b per side = 14,400 flops) were moved into the deskew (lp 'reschedule' form; not done: lockstep form is what the bench proves).
compiler_note.be_control: be_cmd (29 b) lands into every BE region and is padded 12..21 stages (3,828 flops) so each BE's control stays in step with its column (CONTROL_DELAY = BE_DELAY + HOPD x hop unchanged). Alternative (not done): fold the pad into CONTROL_DELAY (BE_DELAY + HOPD x hop + t(BE) - 3).
compiler_note.pad_hotspots: f_rl_p1 / f_bl_p1 / f_rr_p1 / f_br_p1 pads 3 stages x 3,705 b x 2 sides = 22,230 flops in front of the row-pair-1 tiles of columns 3 / 4 (their row-pair-0 neighbour is one landing ahead). A front that launches row-pair 1 three edges later (calendar shift of the p1 launch) removes them.
compiler_note.cost: 56 landings (16 x 1,636 b rin, 16 x 2,069 b bin, 8 x 100 b gather p0->p1, 8 x 29 b be_cmd, 6 x 138 b q chain, 2 x 184 b q -> front): 308,268 landing flops (D 4) + 40,458 pad flops per SM; x16 SMs on d4g ~5.6 M flops. D 2 (LANDING-CONTRACT: valid for 625/632 S81 links) would cut the ring ~40%; decide after die STA dL.
